title: Engine won't shut off
h1: Why does my engine keep running after I turn it off?
metaDesc: Engine keeps running, coughs or diesels after you turn it off? Answer a few questions to find the likely cause, how urgent it is and what to do.
synonyms: engine runs after key is off
engine keeps running after turning off
push button won't turn car off
car says shift to park and won't turn off
fan running after car is off
car still running with key out
intro: An engine that won't shut off can be anything from a normal cooling fan to a shifter that isn't quite in Park to an electrical fault that keeps the engine powered. What you see and hear right after you switch off narrows it down quickly. Answer the questions below for possible causes and the safest next step.
safety: If the engine won't stop in a garage, open the garage door and get everyone out. Exhaust fumes can build up quickly.
If the engine revs higher and higher on its own, get people away from the vehicle and call for help.
If the gas pedal sticks while driving, shift to Neutral, brake firmly, steer to a safe spot, then shut the engine off.

q_what_happens.q: What happens when you turn the key off or press the Start/Stop button?
q_what_happens.help: "Dieseling" (also called run-on) is when an engine keeps coughing and chugging unevenly for a few seconds after you switch it off.

opts.a: The engine keeps running smoothly, even with the key off or removed
The engine coughs, chugs or shakes for a few seconds, then stops
Push-button start: pressing the button doesn't turn it off
The engine stops, but I hear a fan or whirring under the hood
The engine revs higher and higher by itself (diesel engine)

q_after_off.q: Right after you switch off, which fits best?
q_after_off.help: The tachometer is the gauge that shows engine speed (RPM). If it still shows a reading, the engine is still running.

opts.a: The tachometer still shows RPM and exhaust keeps coming out
The dash goes dark, but a fan or pump keeps running under the hood
The engine shakes or coughs briefly, then stops

q_park.q: What does the dashboard show when you press the button to turn it off?

opts.a: A message like "Shift to Park", or the gear display doesn't show P
It shows P with no message, but the button doesn't respond

q_vehicle_type.q: Does the engine have a carburetor or fuel injection?
q_vehicle_type.help: Most cars built since the early 1990s have fuel injection. A carburetor is found mainly on older vehicles, classic cars and some small engines.

q_hot.q: Has the engine been running hotter than usual?

opts.a: Yes, the temperature gauge is high or in the red
No, the temperature gauge is normal

result.title: An electrical fault may be keeping the engine powered
result.now: Don't drive it. Put it in Park with the parking brake on, turn the key to ON and back to OFF firmly, and if it keeps running, call roadside assistance or a mobile mechanic.
if: If you're comfortable with the fuse box, pulling the fuel pump fuse or relay (shown in the owner's manual) will usually make the engine stall within a few seconds.
If it's a manual, you can stall it: with the parking brake on and your foot hard on the brake, put it in a high gear and release the clutch.
If it's in a closed space, open the doors or garage door right away and get everyone out.
If you smell burning plastic or see smoke from the dash, steering column or fuse box, get out, step away and call for help.
result.why: On a modern car, turning the key off cuts power to the fuel and ignition systems. If the engine keeps running normally, something is still feeding that power, often a worn ignition switch or a relay stuck closed. A shop will test the switch, relays and wiring to find which. Until it's fixed, you can't count on being able to shut the engine off.

causes.name: Worn or faulty ignition switch
causes.clues: The key feels loose or different, or the dash and radio act oddly when you jiggle the key.

causes.name: Stuck main or ignition relay
causes.clues: It happens on push-button cars too, sometimes with a click from the fuse box.

causes.name: Wiring fault after a repair or accessory install
causes.clues: It started after a remote starter, alarm or stereo was installed.

you: Note whether the dash lights and radio stay on with the key removed.
Think back to any recent electrical work or accessories added.

result.title: Classic engine run-on (dieseling)
result.now: Make sure the idle isn't set too high, and book a tune-up check when convenient.
if: If it happens mainly after hard driving on hot days, let it idle for 30 seconds before switching off.
If the engine also pings or knocks under load, get it checked sooner, because the same hot spots can damage the engine.
If the temperature gauge is high or in the red, or you smell fuel, don't drive it until it's checked.
result.why: On carbureted engines, fuel can keep getting pulled in after the ignition is off. Hot carbon deposits or a high idle can then ignite it, so the engine chugs on unevenly for a few seconds. It's common on older vehicles and is often fixed with adjustments and cleaning once a shop checks the idle and timing.

causes.name: Idle speed set too high
causes.clues: The idle sounds fast, or the engine was recently adjusted.

causes.name: Carbon buildup in the engine
causes.clues: Lots of short trips, pinging under load, or high mileage.

causes.name: Failed anti-dieseling (idle stop) solenoid
causes.clues: Run-on started suddenly on a carburetor that has one.

causes.name: Fuel octane too low or ignition timing off
causes.clues: Pinging or knocking when accelerating.

you: Check the owner's manual or engine label for the correct fuel grade.
Note whether it happens mainly when the engine is very hot.

result.title: Overheating may be making the engine run on
result.now: Switch the engine off, let it cool completely, and don't drive it until the overheating is fixed. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you see steam or coolant leaking, stay away from the radiator cap. It can spray scalding coolant.
If the coolant is low, don't just top it up and drive. The reason it went low and overheated needs to be found first.
If you hear knocking, or see smoke or a red oil pressure light, don't restart the engine.
result.why: An overheating engine has hot spots that can ignite fuel even after the ignition is off. The run-on is a symptom; the overheating is the bigger danger, and it can warp or crack engine parts.

causes.name: Low coolant or a cooling system leak
causes.clues: Puddles under the car, a sweet smell, or steam.

causes.name: Failed cooling fan, thermostat or water pump
causes.clues: It overheats mostly at idle, or the gauge climbs quickly.

causes.name: Ignition timing or mixture problem
causes.clues: Pinging, poor power, or recent engine adjustments.

you: Once fully cold, check the coolant level.
Look for leaks under the car.
shop: Thermostat, fan and water pump check

result.title: A shake at shutdown on a modern car often points to engine mounts
result.now: Book a check when convenient and mention exactly when the shake happens.
if: If you also feel a clunk when shifting into gear or accelerating, worn engine mounts are more likely. Get them checked sooner.
If the engine truly keeps running after the key is off, or you smell fuel, don't drive it and have it checked right away.
If the check engine light flashes or the temperature gauge runs high, have it checked before driving further.
result.why: Fuel-injected engines cut fuel the moment you switch off, so true run-on is rare. What feels like run-on is often the engine rocking as it stops, which worn mounts let you feel more. Less often, a leaking injector lets fuel in after shutdown. A shop will usually inspect the mounts and check for codes before deciding.

causes.name: Worn engine or transmission mounts
causes.clues: A clunk when shifting into gear, or extra vibration at idle.

causes.name: Leaking fuel injector
causes.clues: A fuel smell, hard starting when warm, or a rough start.

causes.name: Heavy carbon buildup
causes.clues: Pinging under load, or a check engine light.

you: Have someone watch the engine while you switch off and see if it rocks a lot.
Notice any clunk when shifting from Park into Drive or Reverse.

result.title: The car doesn't think it's in Park
result.now: With your foot on the brake, move the shifter out of Park and firmly back into Park, then press the button again.
if: If it keeps happening, have the shifter's Park switch checked soon. Leaving the car in accessory mode can drain the battery.
If the car won't stay in Park or rolls, don't leave it. Set the parking brake and have it checked before driving again.
result.why: Most push-button cars won't fully shut down unless they detect the shifter in Park. A worn switch in the shifter, or something like a coin or spilled drink in the shifter, can stop it from registering Park.

causes.name: Worn or faulty Park position switch in the shifter
causes.clues: Wiggling the shifter makes the message go away.

causes.name: Debris or a spill in the shifter
causes.clues: Something was dropped or spilled near the shifter recently.

causes.name: Shift cable out of adjustment
causes.clues: The gear display doesn't match where the shifter sits.

you: Push the shifter firmly into Park and check the gear display.
Look around the shifter for debris or signs of a spill.
shop: Check for open recalls or service bulletins

result.title: The Start/Stop button or keyless system isn't responding
result.now: Press and hold the Start/Stop button for a few seconds. That shuts off most cars even when a quick press doesn't. Book a check when convenient.
if: If holding the button doesn't shut it off, don't leave it running and don't drive it. Call roadside assistance or a mobile mechanic.
If the key fob battery is weak, replace it. Some cars act oddly when they can't read the fob.
result.why: Push-button systems use a switch and a computer to decide when to shut down. A sticky button, a weak fob battery or a module fault can stop a short press from working, while a long press often overrides it.

causes.name: Worn or sticky Start/Stop button
causes.clues: You have to press harder or more than once.

causes.name: Weak key fob battery
causes.clues: A "key not detected" message, or the remote range has dropped.

causes.name: Keyless ignition module fault
causes.clues: Other odd behavior, like the car not locking or warning lights.

you: Try holding the button down for a few seconds.
Check the owner's manual for the shutdown procedure.
shop: Code scan of the keyless system
Check for software updates or service bulletins

result.title: This sounds like the cooling fan or a pump finishing its job
result.now: Wait up to several minutes. On many cars the radiator fan or an electric coolant pump runs after shutdown to cool the engine, then turns off by itself.
if: If the fan keeps running for a long time or the battery goes flat overnight, have the fan relay checked.
If you see steam or smell coolant, or the temperature gauge was high before you switched off, the engine may be overheating. Have it checked before driving again.
If you smell burning or see smoke, step away from the car.
result.why: Fans and some pumps are controlled separately from the engine and can keep running after a hot drive, especially in warm weather or after towing. This is normal on many cars. A tachometer reading of zero and no exhaust from the tailpipe confirm the engine itself is off.

causes.name: Normal after-run cooling
causes.clues: It happens after hot days or long drives and stops within several minutes.

causes.name: Stuck fan relay or temperature sensor fault
causes.clues: The fan runs for a long time even on a cold engine, or the battery keeps going flat.

causes.name: Engine running hot
causes.clues: The temperature gauge has been higher than usual.

you: Time how long the noise lasts after you switch off.
Check that the tachometer reads zero and no exhaust comes out.

result.title: This may be a diesel engine runaway, which is an emergency
result.now: Get everyone away from the vehicle. If it's a manual and you can do it safely, hold the brakes hard, put it in the highest gear and release the clutch to stall the engine.
if: If there's fire or heavy smoke, move well away and call 911.
If the engine stops, don't restart it. Have it towed to a shop.
Don't reach into the engine bay or try to block the air intake by hand. The engine can pull in loose items and the parts are very hot.
result.why: A diesel engine can keep running and speeding up on fuel it isn't supposed to get, most often engine oil. The key can't shut off that fuel supply, and the engine can overspeed until it fails badly.

causes.name: Oil leaking into the intake from a failed turbocharger seal
causes.clues: Heavy blue or white smoke and a high-pitched whine before it happened.

causes.name: Engine oil overfilled or crankcase vapors pulled into the intake
causes.clues: Oil was recently added or changed.

causes.name: Fuel system or governor fault
causes.clues: The engine revved up without heavy smoke.

shop: Oil level and crankcase ventilation check

result.title: Find out whether the engine is truly still running
result.now: After switching off, watch the tachometer and check for exhaust at the tailpipe. Then book a check and tell the shop what you saw.
if: If the engine clearly keeps running with the key off, don't drive it. Call roadside assistance or a mobile mechanic.
If it's just a fan or whirring noise that stops within several minutes, that's often normal. Mention it to the shop if the temperature gauge has been running high.
result.why: A fan running after shutdown, an engine that coughs briefly and an engine that won't stop at all have very different causes and urgency. A quick look at the gauges and the tailpipe tells them apart.

causes.name: Normal cooling fan after-run
causes.clues: The dash is dark and the noise stops on its own.

causes.name: Engine run-on or shutdown shake
causes.clues: A brief cough or shudder, then silence.

causes.name: Electrical fault keeping the engine powered
causes.clues: The engine keeps running normally with the key out.

you: Record a short video with sound right after you switch off. It helps the shop a lot.
